approach.method_basis: The Parent is a de novo molecular graph optimizer that runs one independent session per objective and never sees anything but that session's own accepted scores. It keeps a population of the 64 best scored molecules, breeds a fresh field of 160 candidates each feedback step by graph crossover and atom- and bond-local mutation drawn from ranked parent quantiles, and admits a candidate to the field only if it parses, canonicalizes to a new identity and duplicates nothing already emitted. It then fits a Gaussian process on the session's accepted molecules alone, using a count-based Morgan fingerprint with a generalized Tanimoto kernel, and buys the announced ten by drawing one correlated sample of the posterior over the whole field and taking the sampled maximum at each position, removing each bought identity before the next. On top of that, an earlier child added the one restriction that has ever paid off here: while three consecutive feedback steps have failed to beat the session's best molecule, only the forty highest predicted-mean members of the field may be bought at all, released by the first improvement. The most recent child simplified admission by deleting a chemistry rule that had been rejecting candidates for introducing unusual sulfur environments, which raised the mean. Everything else - the operators, the single global surrogate, the sampled-maxima buy and its numerical fallback - is as described.
approach.novelty: This node replaces that fixed stall bar with a trust region in the surrogate's own similarity geometry, whose width is driven by whether the search is actually succeeding. Each feedback step the field is ranked by how similar its members are to the molecule the session is currently trying to beat, measured with the same fingerprint kernel the surrogate already uses, and only the most similar R members may be bought. R walks a ladder from the whole field down to the announced batch: one step narrower after a step that fails to beat the incumbent, one step wider after a step that beats it, and when it has narrowed as far as it goes and still fails, the region jumps to the best scored molecule it has not yet been centred on and opens back up to the whole field. Three things make this new here. The eligible set is defined by locality to a moving centre instead of by predicted rank, so exploitation is spatial rather than a re-reading of the same predictions that already price the buy. Its width is carried state updated by observed outcomes rather than a constant switched by a counter, so the restriction tightens the longer the search fails. And it adds a restart, which this loop has never had at all. It is deliberately not the lineage's earlier localization attempt, which also broke the surrogate itself into regional episodes fitted on far fewer records and cost about 0.036 of mean endpoint score: the single global predictor, its full accepted archive, the one shared field and the sampled-maxima pricing rule are all kept exactly as they are, and only who is allowed to be bought changes. No sibling has yet been tried on this Parent, and the earlier attempts to control the bar this node replaces changed only when it is released, keeping the predicted-mean set and a constant size; both lost.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-f28be8ac3d12 spends almost every purchase without moving the thing it is scored on, and the only control it has over which candidates may be bought at all is blind to that. Its own published record over the fifteen matched sessions: 4,350 purchases, of which 255 raised the session incumbent and 4,095 raised it by exactly zero, for a total realized incumbent-increment mass of 6.079659193977185 and a mean of 0.0013976228032131467 per purchase, with a mean posterior-mean rank of 29.17 among 160 admitted members. The inherited eligibility restriction - the one intervention class with a measured gain on this lineage (n-61b9b3bfb40d, 0.607030316211131 against its own code Parent n-1744a1494180) - is a fixed binary bar: a counter of three consecutive non-improving announcements switches on a constant top-forty-of-160 posterior-mean mask. On this Parent it fired in 89 of 435 announcements (890 purchases) and in 77 of those 89 the passive full-field replay over the same drawn rows would have bought a different batch, so it binds and routes real choices; but in the other 346 announcements the buy ranges over the whole admitted field, the restriction never contracts further however long the session fails, never relaxes gradually when it succeeds, and has no restart. The two controller variants tried on it changed only when it is released and both lost (n-c7eb0cb7da3b 0.5991008470153286, n-5911390da209 0.6064683335873687 against 0.607030316211131). The limiting behaviour is therefore the control law over the eligible set, not the predictor, the field or the pricing rule: nothing has made the size of the eligible set a function of realized success, and nothing has defined that set by locality to the molecule the session is actually trying to beat.

adoptions.applicability: Adopted on this Parent because eligibility restriction is the only intervention class with a measured gain on this lineage while its size and trigger have never responded to realized progress; the paper high dimensional continuous setting and its convergence and regret statements do not transfer to fifteen 300-evaluation discrete molecular sessions.
adoptions.borrowed_element: A trust region centred on the incumbent whose extent is adapted by explicit success and failure counting, expanded after an improving round, contracted after a failing one, and restarted elsewhere once it has collapsed to its floor and still fails.

deviations.adopted_setting: A rank set in the inherited count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto kernel: the R members of the admitted field most similar to the centre, ties broken by pool index.
deviations.paper_setting: A hyperrectangle in a continuous box-constrained domain, with per-dimension side lengths scaled by the fitted lengthscales.
deviations.reason: The decision set is a freshly generated discrete molecular graph field with no box geometry or dimensions; the kernel the surrogate already uses is the only locality this method owns, and adding a learned encoder would need a new pretrained asset.

deviations.adopted_setting: A fixed five-level ladder 160/80/40/20/10, one level per announcement, floored at the announced batch of ten and bound before evaluation.
deviations.paper_setting: Continuous halving and doubling of the side length between a minimum and a maximum, after runs of several consecutive successes or failures.
deviations.reason: A discrete field of 160 admits only integer set sizes, the floor must leave ten distinct identities so the announced batch is always fillable, and the ladder is made to contain the inherited forty so the measured difference is the control law and not the value. One step per announcement is chosen because a session has only 29 of them.

deviations.adopted_setting: One region at a time over one shared field, with one global surrogate fitted to the whole accepted archive, and a restart that moves the single centre.
deviations.paper_setting: Several trust regions run in parallel with an implicit bandit allocation across them, each with its own local surrogate fitted to nearby data.
deviations.reason: The parallel localized form was already measured on this lineage and lost 0.0356 of mean endpoint score because each episode refitted from far fewer records (n-bc1f80092068); only the controller is adopted, and the oracle budget is unchanged.

adoptions.implementation_change: Evolution carries region_level on the bound ladder 160/80/40/20/10 with region_centre; the controller at the end of Evolution.observe steps one level per announcement from the realized improving flag, floors at ten and, on a collapse, re-centres on the best accepted molecule not yet used as a centre and resets to 160. FingerprintPosterior.select restricts the eligible set to the R members most similar to the centre.

adoptions.applicability: Applies directly because this optimizer already owns a fitted similarity kernel over molecular graphs and the centre is always an accepted member of the archive the kernel is fitted on, so the region needs no new model, asset or fit.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Defining the trust region of a structured-input optimizer through the model own learned similarity structure instead of a geometric box.

deviations.adopted_setting: The fixed inherited count-Morgan fingerprint kernel of the session-local Gaussian process, unchanged and not retrained.
deviations.paper_setting: A trained deep-kernel variational autoencoder latent space, with the encoder updated jointly with the surrogate during optimization.
deviations.reason: A new pretrained asset is forbidden in this campaign, a frozen-prior proposal source was already measured as a loss on this lineage, and keeping the kernel fixed is what makes the eligibility change attributable.

deviations.adopted_setting: The region constrains only which already admitted candidates may be bought; generation, the operators and the 160-member refill are untouched.
deviations.paper_setting: The trust region constrains where new candidates are generated and decoded.
deviations.reason: Proposal-side changes are the axis with the most repeated counterexamples on this lineage, and restricting only the eligible set is what keeps this a single attributable intervention on the consumer the ticket targets.

adoptions.implementation_change: FingerprintPosterior.select computes one row of the existing count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto kernel between the centre and the admitted field from cached fingerprints and ranks the field by (-centre_similarity, pool_index).

literature_review.conclusion: Reused from the frozen round-80 bottleneck review r80-exhausted-axes-review, which is the recorded basis of this ticket under the recorded stagnation; no new web search was needed because no model, asset or package is introduced. Of the two sources behind its trust-region method, exactly one element is taken: the success/failure size controller with a collapse restart, with locality expressed in the surrogate's own kernel because the decision set is a discrete molecular field. Everything the lineage has already measured as a loss is deliberately not adopted - localized predictors and regional episodes, latent encoders, generation-side restriction and removal of the sampled residual - and the paper convergence and regret claims transfer to nothing here.

sources.applicability: The success/failure size controller with a collapse restart is the element this lineage never built, and it is the whole of what is adopted here. The single global surrogate and its full accepted archive are kept, because localizing the predictor was measured as a loss on this line (n-bc1f80092068).
sources.finding: A global stationary surrogate over-explores because it assumes one lengthscale everywhere; the paper instead restricts each decision to a trust region centred on the best point found so far and adapts that region size with explicit success and failure counters, expanding after improvements, contracting after failures and restarting the region when it collapses. The controller, not a model change, is what the paper credits for beating global BO.
sources.title: Scalable Global Optimization via Local Bayesian Optimization (TuRBO), Eriksson et al., NeurIPS 2019

sources.applicability: It is the reason locality here is a rank in the surrogate own kernel rather than a hyperrectangle: this search space is a discrete set of generated molecular graphs with no box geometry. The paper autoencoder and latent search are not adopted, since a new pretrained asset is forbidden in this campaign.
sources.finding: Trust regions from high-dimensional continuous BO are carried over to structured inputs such as molecules, where locality has to be defined through a learned encoder or deep kernel rather than through a box; the authors report large improvements over prior latent-space molecular BO and conclude that the optimization strategy matters as much as the model.
sources.title: Local Latent Space Bayesian Optimization over Structured Inputs (LOL-BO), Maus et al., NeurIPS 2022

hypothesis: One replacement of the eligibility consumer of the allocator: a closed-loop eligibility region over the same admitted field. Locality to the session's current centre in the inherited count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto kernel decides which members may be bought, and the region's size is carried integer state updated once per announcement from realized success and failure, with an explicit re-centring restart at the floor. Per announcement the 160-member admitted field is ranked by similarity to the centre, ties broken by pool index, and the eligible set is the R most similar members. R lives on the ladder 160, 80, 40, 20, 10, starts at 160, moves one step down after an announcement that does not improve the session incumbent, one step up after one that does, and never below ten, so a batch of ten distinct identities is always fillable. When R is already at ten and the announcement still does not improve, the centre moves to the highest-scoring accepted molecule of the session that has not yet been a centre and R resets to 160. The centre is the session's own incumbent - highest accepted score, earliest serial on ties - except while a collapse has pinned it to a lower unused molecule, and it returns to the incumbent on the next improving announcement. The inherited K=3 stall counter and its top-forty posterior-mean mask are still computed every announcement as a passive contrast and gate nothing. The predictor, its full accepted archive, the single fresh field, the correlated draw, the sampled-maxima pricing, the sequential availability masking and its tie rule, the numerical fallback, every graph operator and all admission and duplicate rules are retained verbatim. The path of effect: the eligible set is spatially concentrated around the molecule the session is trying to beat exactly when the session is failing, so purchases land on near neighbours of the incumbent instead of anywhere in the field, which should convert more of the 4,350 purchases into realized incumbent increments; when the session is succeeding the region stays at the whole field and the allocator behaves exactly as the Parent does.

finding_summary.headline: The locality region ran exactly and concentrated the buy, but progress mass fell 6.08 to 5.39 and the panel lost 0.046
finding_summary.insights: Eligibility restriction was the one intervention class with a measured gain on this lineage, and the open question was whether the fixed stall bar was merely the first setting tried. This node answers the locality form of that question negatively, with the mechanism verified rather than assumed: redefining the eligible set by kernel locality around a moving centre and making its width closed-loop state with a restart is fully exercised - more than twice the Parent's restricted exposure, 95.8 per cent of binding announcements buying a different batch, purchase similarity ranks cut from 54 to 34 - and still loses 0.046 of endpoint mean and 0.690 of progress mass. The campaign can stop treating 'control the eligible set harder' as an untested hope on this host; what remains untested is a narrowing that is not centred on the incumbent. Three measured things explain the failure and are worth carrying forward. First, the loss profile is the opposite of the predicted one: the node bought more incumbent improvements than the Parent (268 against 255) and less total progress, so narrowing to the incumbent's neighbourhood reliably buys small analogue gains and gives up the rare large jump this panel's endpoint actually depends on - visible as one Objective losing in all three seeds and as a single 0.247 Parent increment on another that the child never found. Second, the restriction is not an independent information channel: purchases under the region sat at mean posterior-mean rank 26.2 against the Parent's 29.17, so the kernel neighbourhood of the incumbent largely contains the members the surrogate already prices highest, and the controller mostly removed the field's tail rather than redirecting the buy. Third, the restart is nominal. All 23 collapses re-centred, but the replacement centre was exactly as good as the incumbent it replaced in 14 of 23 events (median score gap 0.000, mean 0.0037) and a one- or two-atom analogue of it, because 'the best accepted molecule not yet used as a centre' in a 290-record archive is a halogen permutation of the molecule that just failed; the Molecular reading of the same sessions shows the same thing from the chemistry side, with one session's fifty best products collapsing to twenty-five graphs under halogen identification and carrying only eighteen distinct scores, and the enriched end of most sessions sitting on a single Murcko scaffold. The method limitation this exposes is not a ladder value: a restart whose centre is chosen by score rank over an archive dominated by near-duplicates cannot leave the neighbourhood it is trying to escape, and a region defined by the surrogate's own kernel is redundant with the ranking it is meant to correct. Removing it needs a different kind of component - a restart or centre criterion defined by dissimilarity or scaffold novelty against the centres already used, a proposal operator that can make a scaffold-level jump instead of reaching it through single-atom edits, or a ranking model better than the one in place (batch predicted-versus-realized rank correlation was 0.514 here against 0.518 in the Parent, unchanged and only moderately informative) - rather than another step, floor or width. A measurement lesson also falls out: the registered mechanistic endpoint was not independent of the score. Incumbent-increment mass telescopes to final best minus initial best, and the ten initial records are shared, so each cell's mass delta equals its score delta exactly; the mechanistic prediction and the score prediction could not have disagreed. Future eligibility experiments on this lineage need an endpoint that can. Two things stay open. The size of the loss is not separable from path dispersion at panel level: -0.046 lies inside the law-free re-draw band recorded for this host family ([-0.055, +0.015]), so the sign is carried by three negative seeds and a repeated single-Objective loss rather than by the panel magnitude, and that band is a departure width, not a confidence interval. And nothing here prices the parts: deactivating the inherited bar and installing the region happened together, so this is no isolated price for the mask it replaces, and the region definition, the success/failure ladder and the re-centring restart were replaced as one unit.
finding_summary.results: The controller ran exactly as registered in all fifteen matched sessions, and the registered endpoint moved the wrong way. Execution: all 435 announcements carry region state, and the realized ladder never once broke the bound rule (0 violations of the one-step-per-announcement rule, the floor of ten, the collapse condition or the reset). The eligible set stood at the whole field of 160 in 197 announcements, at 80 in 112, at 40 in 60, at 20 in 38 and at the floor of ten in 28; every one of the fifteen sessions visited at least two ladder levels, against a registered minimum of twelve of fifteen; 213 contractions, 95 expansions, 104 holds and 23 resets. All 23 collapses re-centred on an accepted molecule that had not been a centre, with none exhausted, against a structurally zero Parent count. The region restricted the buy in 238 of 435 announcements against the Parent's 89, covering 2,380 purchases against 890, and in 228 of those 238 the realized ten differed from the inherited stall rule replayed over the same drawn posterior rows (Parent 77 of 89), displacing 1,103 identities. The inherited top-forty posterior-mean bar was computed in all 435 announcements and gated nothing: its counter fired in 90, in all 90 the eligible set was the similarity region rather than the mean-ranked forty, and in 19 of them the buy still ranged over the whole field, which the Parent's rule would have forbidden. Direct behaviour moved as predicted: the mean similarity rank of the identities actually purchased was 34.4 of 160 against 54.2 for the same announcements at full width (lower in 15 of 15 cells), 21.7 against 56.3 inside restricted announcements, and monotone in the contraction - 50.9 at level 160, 30.9 at 80, 16.4 at 40, 9.2 at 20 and 4.5 at the floor - with mean kernel similarity of purchases to the centre 0.81. Nothing else moved: the first announced pool and all ten of its purchases are identical to the Parent's in every cell, divergence begins at the first announcement whose region bound, all 197 full-width announcements reproduce the retained sampled-maxima law on the same drawn rows, and no announcement took the numerical fallback. The registered useful-transfer endpoint failed. Realized incumbent-increment mass over the fifteen equal sessions was 5.390 against the Parent's 6.080, short by 0.690, and only 6 of 15 cells exceeded their Parent cell. Inside the node, the 2,380 purchases made while the region bound carried 1.497 of that mass, 0.00063 per purchase, while the 1,970 purchases made at full width carried 3.893, 0.00198 per purchase. The node produced more incumbent improvements than the Parent, 268 against 255 of 4,350 purchases, but smaller ones: what went missing is the rare large jump. Endpoint scores followed the mass. The paired macro mean is 0.5678 against the Parent's 0.6138, -0.0460 on all fifteen matched cells, with every seed negative (-0.0610, -0.0512, -0.0258) and the registered minimum of +0.002 not attained. The loss is concentrated: sitagliptin_mpo lost in all three seeds (-0.133, -0.273, -0.118) and deco_hop lost 0.248 on seed 0, where the Parent found one 0.247 increment the child never matched (its largest there was 0.008); median_2 and zaleplon_mpo gained slightly on most seeds and drd2_docking was flat within 0.007.

molecular.headline: Flat, ring-rich aromatic series whose score climbs on N-F, O-F, O-Br and S-Cl attachments, with no stereochemistry and no CF3 anywhere
molecular.overall_character:
Scope and provenance. This reads the molecules of n-84885e74a0d7 on all five objectives and frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, against its code Parent n-f28be8ac3d12 on the same matched cells. context.comparison records child_complete=true and paired_complete=true with matched seeds 0/1/2, so both arms are complete; no comparison is missing and context.molecular_digest.tasks_without_trajectories is empty. All fifteen Child trajectories exist under .worktrees/slot-0/runs/staging/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories/ and all fifteen published Parent trajectories under runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-f28be8ac3d12/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories/; each file holds 300 accepted observations, ten shared initials and 290 optimizer products, i.e. 870 optimizer products per objective and 4,350 per arm. Every paired session starts from the same ten initial identities and scores. Readings below are molecule-level RDKit 2023.09.6 perception over those exact files (scratch scripts in the agent scratch directory); the digest's own counters are SMILES-text readings and agree with them. The trajectories record purchased candidates only, not the unbought field.

What the generator makes. Medium-sized, flat, heavily decorated aromatic chemistry. Mean heavy-atom counts per objective are 24.5, 33.1, 30.8, 32.6 and 25.9 with medians 25-33; perceived rings average 3.1-4.8 and aromatic rings 2.0-3.9; the digest's ring_closure_rate is 0.974-0.994 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.969-0.990, so ring and aromatic content is genuinely rich rather than nominal. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry frameworks do appear: indole-2-carboxanilides (an indole substructure in 440/870 products on one objective, an amide in 736/870), aryloxy-pyridines and fused pyrimidinone/oxazinone heteroaromatics, saturated 1,4-diazepane and piperazine-like amines fused to benzazepine and chromane-type systems, xanthine-like pyrrolopyrimidine-2,4-diones, and fused carbazole/pyridazinone lactams. Branching is near-universal (branch_rate 0.969-0.993) and halogenation is heavy (halogen_rate 0.88-0.98 on four of five objectives, 0.11 on the fifth).

What is wrong with them. Three absences are absolute across all 4,350 products: no stereochemistry is ever written (zero '@' or '@@' tokens in any of the fifteen files, matching the digest's stereocentre_rate of 0.0), no trifluoromethyl group is ever formed (zero matches of [CX4](F)(F)F, although 97 products place two fluorines on one carbon, 89 of them bonded to nitrogen as an aminal), and no azole of the triazole/tetrazole class appears. Formal charge is effectively absent too: eight charged-atom tokens in two products out of 4,350. Against that, the highest-scoring ends of four of the five searches are enriched in attachments a chemist would reject: nitrogen- and oxygen-halogen bonds, N-halo amides and amidines, aromatic N-fluorination, hypofluorites and hypobromites, sulfenyl and disulfenyl chlorides, peroxides, cyanate esters, oxime ethers, and gem-difluoro aminals. On one objective 483/870 products (55.5%) carry at least one such bond and the proportion rises inside the best fifty; on another 510/870 carry an N-halogen bond and 49 of the 50 best carry an aromatic one. Size discipline also fails at both tails: 86 products across the five sessions have six or fewer heavy atoms (single atoms and diatomics among them, 14 of them purchased at evaluation 250 or later), and 23 products have 60 or more heavy atoms, up to 107, with the digest's max_smiles_length reaching 204.

Breadth. Whole-session Murcko scaffold counts are 168, 302, 335, 511 and 221 per 870 products, so the searches are not globally collapsed, and every one of those counts is below the paired Parent session (232, 388, 350, 579, 292). The narrowness is at the enriched end: the best fifty products hold 8, 4, 28, 37 and 14 scaffolds, and in 7 of the 15 sessions the best twenty products sit on four scaffolds or fewer (two sessions on a single one). Where the Parent reached chemistry this node did not, it was a different exotic family rather than a cleaner one: a thioxo-purinone-like fused polycycle bearing a quinazoline on one objective, and a non-aromatic polyfluorinated cyclopentene/fluoroazetidine series on another. Scoring, ranking and activation are not this report's to judge; this is a description of output chemistry only.

per_task.generated_character: Compact, flat indole-2-carboxanilides. 870 optimizer products average 24.5 heavy atoms (median 25, range 1-35), 3.11 perceived rings and 2.64 aromatic rings; 852/870 contain a benzene ring, 736 an amide, 440 an indole substructure and 802 an aryl halide. Mean QED is 0.523 and mean SA score 3.0, so the bulk of the set looks like ordinary small-molecule chemistry. The enriched end is one series: 37 of the best 50 share the Murcko scaffold O=C(Nc1ccccc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1, and seed 0's best twenty products sit on a single scaffold. Nitriles and esters are all but absent (2 and 4 of 870), ketones appear in 34, and no sulfur-oxygen group occurs at all (0/870).
liabilities: N-fluoro amides in 95/870 products, including every member of the top score plateau (C(=O)N(F)c1ccccc1).
N-hydroxy and N-O-fluoro pyrrole nitrogens: n2O in the plateau and n2OF at 0.4344 (CCc1c(N)cc2c(c1C)c(Cl)c(C(=O)N(F)c1ccccc1)n2OF).
Benzylic halides (ArCH2Cl/Br/F) in 159/870 products and 22 of the best 50; chloromethyl arenes are alkylators, not substituents.
Benzo-fused four-membered nitrogen rings in 143/870 products, including the session-final series COc1c2c(cc3c1N3C)CC(C(=O)CN(N)c1ccc(Cl)cc1)=C2.
Score-degenerate halogen permutation spends purchases without moving the score (three plateau members differing only F/Cl/Br).
Four products of six or fewer heavy atoms were still being purchased after evaluation 250.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-84885e74a0d7 against code Parent n-f28be8ac3d12; the frozen five-session Search panel, seeds 0/1/2, 290 accepted optimizer observations per session, 4,350 per arm, files under .worktrees/slot-0/runs/staging/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories/ and runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-f28be8ac3d12/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories/. Zero '@' or '@@' tokens occur in any of the fifteen Child files, matching the digest stereocentre_rate of 0.0 in every session. In the 50 highest-scoring products of one session RDKit 2023.09.6 finds 131 potential tetrahedral centres with none assigned and every one of those 50 products has at least one; two further sessions give 69 and 35 unassigned centres over their best 50. The Parent shows the same absence, so this is a lineage property, not a change.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator never specifies stereochemistry, even when it builds stereogenic carbons and saturated ring fusions on purpose.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Configuration has to become an explicit, mutable degree of freedom in the representation and the edit vocabulary: proposals should be able to set, flip and inherit atom and bond stereo separately from connectivity, and the identity/duplicate rule has to treat two configurations of the same graph as different candidates. Without that, a whole axis of chemistry is invisible to the feedback loop regardless of what is being optimized.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one session 483 of 870 products carry at least one N-halogen, O-halogen, S-halogen, peroxide, N-O, cyanate ester, oxime-ether or gem-difluoro-aminal bond, and the proportion rises at the enriched end: of its 50 best, 34 carry a difluoro aminal, 31 an aromatic N-halogen, 25 an oxime ether, 23 an O-halogen, 14 a cyanate ester and 12 an S-halogen. In another session 510/870 products carry an N-halogen bond and 49 of the 50 best do, with 51 hypofluorites. A third session puts N-fluorine on 95 amide nitrogens and an N-O single bond in 73 products, including its entire top score plateau. The same classes are present in the Parent arm (for example 0.431 N-halogen and 0.247 peroxide rates in two of its sessions), so the capability is inherited.
transferable_gaps.gap: Score is climbed by attaching halogens and heteroatoms to heteroatoms rather than by changing the carbon framework, so the best products carry bonds no chemist would make.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The edit vocabulary needs attachment-level chemistry, not atom-level substitution: substituents drawn from a vocabulary of realizable groups attached at plausible positions, with heteroatom-heteroatom and heteroatom-halogen bond formation reachable but rare rather than a default move. The decisive point is that accepted-score feedback alone does not penalise these attachments, so the proposal distribution, not the acceptance rule, has to carry the constraint.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across all 4,350 optimizer products of this node there are zero matches of [CX4](F)(F)F and zero triazole or tetrazole rings, although 97 products place two fluorines on one carbon and 89 of those attach that carbon to nitrogen as an aminal. One session contains no piperidine, piperazine or morpholine at all and another contains a single piperidine, despite halogen-bearing aromatic cores and digest halogen_rate of 0.92 and 0.88, and a third carries its only saturated amine as a four-membered ring (84 azetidines and 74 unsaturated azetines, 19 of its 50 best products containing a four-membered ring). A further session contains 2 nitriles and 4 esters in 870 products and no sulfur-oxygen group at all.
transferable_gaps.gap: Whole classes of ordinary substituent and ring chemistry are simply unreachable: no trifluoromethyl, no azole bioisostere, and no saturated six-membered amine ring in the sessions that need lipophilic or nitrogen-rich decoration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs a fragment or substituent library that spans the common medicinal-chemistry groups as single atomic edits, so that adding three fluorines to one carbon, swapping a ring for a five-membered azole, or growing a six-membered saturated amine are each one move rather than an unreachable sequence. Reaching them only by chains of single-atom substitutions is why the search substitutes implausible neighbours that are one edit away.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Eight charged-atom tokens appear in two of 4,350 products; the digest charged_rate is 0.0 in four sessions and 0.0023 in the fifth. In the one session where a basic aliphatic amine is clearly rewarded it appears in 723/870 products and in all 50 of the best, always drawn as a neutral amine, while the lowest-scoring products of that same session, 0.0002 to 0.0016, are sulfonyl amides with no basic centre at all.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no ionizable or charged state, so protonation and zwitterion chemistry is unexplored even where its own best products are built around a basic amine.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation needs a defined protonation convention and the ability to vary it as an edit, so that basic and acidic centres can be proposed, compared and scored as distinct states rather than collapsed into one neutral drawing.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one session the 50 highest-scoring products are 50 distinct SMILES but only 25 distinct graphs once halogen type is identified, and they carry only 18 distinct score values; three of them differ solely by Cl, Br and F and all score exactly 0.46307504758241197. A second session's 50 best hold 23 distinct score values over 50 products, and its best twenty in one seed sit on a single Murcko scaffold. Over whole sessions the halogen-type collapse removes 110 and 87 products of 870 in two sessions, so the waste is concentrated where the search is already converged.
transferable_gaps.gap: At the enriched end the proposal distribution spends purchases on substituent-identity permutations the stored feedback cannot distinguish.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The proposal step should recognise edits that are indistinguishable to its own accepted feedback and spend the budget on skeleton-level changes instead: deduplicate candidates under substituent-type equivalence before purchase, or require that a batch contain a bounded number of same-scaffold substituent permutations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 86 of the 4,350 products have six or fewer heavy atoms, among them single atoms and diatomics, and 14 of those were purchased at evaluation 250 or later; one session bought three of them as its final six observations, scoring 0.0079, 0.0106 and 0.0092 alongside products above 0.97. At the other tail 23 products carry 60 or more heavy atoms, up to 107, with digest max_smiles_length reaching 204, and the largest are repeated concatenations that score below their own compact series. The Parent arm shows the same two tails (for example 100 products at six or fewer heavy atoms and 27 at 60 or more).
transferable_gaps.gap: Proposal size stays incoherent at both tails for the whole session, including the last batches.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Contraction and regrowth must be constructive and connectivity-preserving: a deletion should keep a connected ring-and-polar core rather than reduce a molecule to a fragment, and a growth step should not concatenate whole copies of a scaffold. Both tails should remain observable so the capability can be measured rather than hidden.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One session carries a four-membered ring in 148/870 products, 143 of them fused directly onto an aromatic ring, and that benzo-fused azetidine motif is what its final six observations are built on. Another has 19 of its 50 best products containing a four-membered ring, 16 of them the unsaturated 2-azetine. A third has 20 of its 50 best carrying a four-membered spiro ring. Three-membered rings appear in only 20 products across the arm, so the preference is specifically for strained four-membered rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-forming edits reach for strained and unsaturated small rings as cheap decoration instead of stable five- and six-membered rings.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction and ring-closure moves need a ring-plausibility preference, favouring five- and six-membered saturated and aromatic rings and treating strained or unsaturated small rings and aromatic-fused four-membered rings as rare proposals, so that ring edits explore skeleton space rather than add an unstable appendage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Whole-session Murcko scaffold counts are 168, 302, 335, 511 and 221 per 870 products, each below the paired Parent session (232, 388, 350, 579, 292), while the 50 best products per session hold only 8, 4, 28, 37 and 14 scaffolds; in 7 of the 15 sessions the best twenty products sit on four scaffolds or fewer and in two of them on a single scaffold. Two seeds of the same session converged on entirely different best families scoring within 0.002 of each other, so comparably good alternatives existed and each session kept only one.
transferable_gaps.gap: Enriched regions reduce to a few decorated scaffolds per session, and the ability to sustain an alternative scaffold while it is still scoring worse is not evident.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The search needs a proposal and retention path for scaffold-level alternatives that is not conditioned on them already scoring better: maintain more than one framework family concurrently and let peripheral decoration compete within each, so that a frontier is a set of skeletons rather than one skeleton with substituent noise.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
